newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - May 22.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following items on its front page on May 22:

WASHINGTON - The Senate voted 55 to 45 to defeat a bipartisan proposal to use an increase in the cigarette tax to expand health care coverage for low-income children after Republican leaders and President Clinton warned that the measure would breach the balanced budget plan.

WASHINGTON - Growing up in a family of 10 girls and one boy, Rep. Anne Meagher Northup learned early in life that sometimes the best way to get along is to go along, and that is the way she is approaching her first months in the House as a republican from Louisville.

WASHINGTON - Montgomery County Executive Douglas Duncan said he would file an appeal with the Federal Communications Commission against a 9.5 percent rate increase that will boost cable television bills by $3 a month.

DENVER - Just 18 days after they began, prosecutors concluded their lean and emotionally riveting case against Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh, who faces the death penalty if he is found guilty of the April 1995 bombing.

WASHINGTON - The Clinton administration is facing renewed pressure to release an overdue report on mercury that suggests the metal is a more potent and widespread health threat than previously was believed.

WASHINGTON - When the Federal Aviation Administration announced last fall that it was looking for someone new to operate its computer systems for payroll, personnel and flight safety, several of the industry's biggest players came knocking. But the winner turned out to be the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

PARIS - French voters are preparing to cast ballots on Sunday in a two-round sequence of national elections that may determine whether France will join Europe in curtailing its welfare state or remain a bastion of government-financed social solidarity.
